headline: Tissue transcriptomics and machine learning nominate disease-linked gene signatures
label: Tissue Transcriptomic Signature Discovery
summary: Recent 2026 studies pair scRNA-seq and bulk transcriptomics with LASSO, SVM-RFE, or SHAP models to prioritize candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of integrated transcriptomic data, often single-cell RNA-seq combined with bulk cohorts, followed by machine learning feature selection (LASSO, SVM-RFE, random forest, SHAP) to nominate candidate genes, cell populations, or metabolites in diseased tissue. Several items apply this to vascular disease: an ACKR1+ endothelial lactate-immune signature in carotid plaque, and THBS1+ macrophages with a THBS1-CD36 axis in coronary atherosclerosis. Fibrosis studies extend the pattern to MMP7 with uridine in pulmonary fibrosis, AREG+ dendritic cells in renal ischemia-reperfusion injury, and conserved fibroblast subsets shared by osteoarthritis synovium and systemic sclerosis skin. The EndoMT R package offers a resource for directional UP/DOWN enrichment analysis, benchmarked on bulk and single-cell data. Other items, including proteomics of kidney tubulointerstitium and DNA methylation of aortic wall, are heterogeneous and do not share this computational framing.
